seo.metaTitle: Newman Car Accident Help | Free Case Review
seo.metaDescription: Injured in a Newman car accident? Get a free case review from our team in Stanislaus County. No fee unless you recover.

hero.subtitle: If a crash on N Street, Balsam Drive, or Merced Street left you hurt, we can help you understand your options at no cost.

about.title: Newman Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Newman is a small, close-knit Stanislaus County community, but its streets still see their share of injury collisions. Public records show 7 injury crashes and 8 injured people in the most recent final reporting year, with Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. showing up more often than other times. Corridors like N Street, Balsam Drive, Inyo Avenue, and Merced Street carry a good portion of local traffic, and that volume brings risk. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the moments right after matter: photos, witness names, and medical records can fade or disappear quickly. We listen to what happened and review your situation to explain your options. There's no cost to talk, and no obligation to move forward until you're ready.
about.ctaText: Tell us what happened — get your free case review today.

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road crew or county vehicle — was involved. Our team can help you figure out which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you were partly at fault for the crash; your compensation is simply reduced by your share of responsibility. That means a disputed intersection near N Street or Balsam Drive doesn't automatically end your claim.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, and we work on contingency — meaning there's no fee unless you recover. That's why it costs nothing to have your case reviewed.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally safer to avoid giving a detailed recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. Our team can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened on a city street like N Street or Merced Street?
items.answer: Crashes on well-traveled Newman corridors like N Street, Balsam Drive, Inyo Avenue, or Merced Street are handled the same way as any other collision under California law, though road design or maintenance issues can sometimes raise separate questions. We can look at the specifics of where and how your crash occurred. If a government entity is involved, shorter deadlines may apply.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. Our team provides a free case review, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover money. There's no obligation to move forward after your initial conversation.
